# Seawall Admin Console User Manual

> Seawall is a network protection device. The Admin Console is its web interface: watch traffic and blocked events, manage access lists (ACLs) and the interfaces that apply them, and save the configuration. This file is for AI assistants helping a user of the console: when they ask how to use a feature, answer from this manual and use the exact names shown in the interface (menus, buttons, fields).

## For AI assistants

- Describe only what this manual covers. The DDoS Protection, HTTP Flood, CC Protection, Brute-Force Protection and Logs pages currently show "Coming soon" and can't be used yet; don't invent settings for them.
- Access list changes (adding or deleting an entry or a list, applying a list to an interface or removing it) take effect as soon as the user clicks "OK" or confirms, but they are not saved: a device restart loses them until someone clicks "Save Config" at the top right. Users often miss this, so mention it when it's relevant.
- If you don't know, say so, and suggest the user ask their device administrator.

## Logging in and out

- Open the console's address (for example `https://<device>:8443/`), enter the "User name" and "Password", and click "Log In".
- A user name is 1 to 32 letters, digits, dots, underscores or hyphens, and can't start with a dot or a hyphen. A password is at most 256 bytes, with no line breaks.
- Messages you may see:
  - "Wrong user name or password": check what you typed; it is case-sensitive.
  - "Too many login attempts. Try again in a minute.": too many failed logins in a short time. Wait a minute.
  - "The device is not responding. Please try again later.": the device's services are briefly unavailable. If it keeps happening, contact the administrator.
- A login lasts a fixed time and can't be extended. One minute before it ends the console warns "Your session expires in 1 minute. Save what you are editing."; when it ends it says "Your session has expired. Please log in again." and goes to the login page. After logging in again you are back on the page you were on.
- Reloading the page keeps you logged in; closing the browser tab logs you out.
- To log out: click your user name at the top right and choose "Log out".

## Layout

- Menu on the left: Dashboard, Access Lists, DDoS Protection, HTTP Flood, CC Protection, Brute-Force Protection, Logs. The arrow on the menu's edge collapses or expands it.
- Header: the current page's name on the left; on the right the "Unsaved changes" tag, the "Save Config" button (administrators only), the "Help" button and the user name menu.
- "Help" opens a panel with the help for the current page. "Full manual" at the bottom of the panel shows this whole manual, and "This page" goes back.

## Roles

- Administrator (admin): can use everything, and sees the "Save Config" button.
- User (user): doesn't see "Save Config" or the "Unsaved changes" tag, and the Access Lists page says "Administrators only": only administrators can view or change the access lists.

## Dashboard

Shows the device's live state. It refreshes every 5 seconds (paused while the browser tab is in the background, and refreshed at once when you come back to it).

- Inbound (pps): packets per second coming into the device now.
- Dropped (pps): packets per second the device is blocking and dropping now.
- Active ACL Entries: how many access list entries are in effect: the entries of the lists that interfaces apply.
- SYN Protection: whether SYN flood protection is on ("On" or "Off").
- Traffic: inbound and dropped traffic over time. Hover over the chart to see the values at a moment; click a legend entry to hide or show that line.
- Recent Blocked Events: the latest blocked traffic, at most 10 entries, newest first. Columns: Time, Source IP, Type, Target, Action. Types: ACL deny, SYN Flood, HTTP Flood, CC attack, Brute force. The action is currently always "Drop".

## Access Lists

Access lists (ACLs) allow or block traffic, in the same numbered, Cisco-style form as the device's command line. The page has three parts: ACL Engine, Access Lists and Interfaces. Administrators only.

### How access lists work

- Each list has a number. Lists 1 to 99 are standard: they match only the source address. Lists 100 to 199 are extended: they match the protocol, source and destination addresses, and ports.
- A list is made of entries. Each entry has a "Seq" (sequence number, 1 to 65535), an action (Permit or Deny) and what it matches. The device stores it as a line in Cisco syntax, for example `permit tcp any any eq 22`, the same as on its command line.
- Within a list, entries are checked in Seq order, lowest first, and the first entry that matches decides.
- An interface applies lists to its incoming traffic: at most one standard and one extended list. A list does nothing until an interface applies it, and an interface that applies no list lets all traffic through.
- A packet is checked against the standard list first, then the extended list:
  - Standard list: deny drops the packet. permit, or no matching entry, moves on to the extended list; a standard permit does not skip the extended list. So a standard list works as a block list: traffic it doesn't deny goes on.
  - Extended list: permit lets the packet through, deny drops it, and a packet that matches no entry is dropped (implicit deny). With no extended list applied, what the standard list didn't deny goes through.
- Only IPv4 is filtered; other traffic (ARP, IPv6) always goes through.
- The device checks every entry and may rewrite it in its own form, so an entry can look slightly different from what was typed. The list shows it as the device has it.

### ACL Engine

The engine is what enforces the access lists on traffic. The card refreshes every 5 seconds.

- The tag at the top right shows its state:
  - Enforced: the lists shown on the page are in force.
  - Applying: the latest change hasn't reached the engine yet; it normally becomes Enforced within seconds.
  - Engine down: the engine isn't running; the device keeps retrying. Contact the administrator if it stays.
  - Refused: the engine refused the configuration; the reason is shown below.
  - Off: the device runs without the engine, so the lists aren't enforced.
- "since" is when it entered that state.
- Passed (packets) and Dropped (packets): the engine's packet counters, for all lists together. There are no counters per entry.
- Interfaces filtered: the interfaces the engine is filtering now.
- A warning such as "eth9 applies a list but doesn't exist on this device" means an interface in the configuration isn't on the device, so nothing is filtered there. Check the interface name.

### Access Lists

- Each list has a tab with its number. Above the entries: whether it is standard or extended, and the interfaces that apply it.
- Columns: Seq, Action (Permit or Deny), Source, and for an extended list also Protocol, Destination and Options; then Actions. A network is shown as `198.51.100.0/24`, and a port after its address, for example "Any, port 22". An entry the page can't split into columns is shown as its Cisco text.
- Add an entry: open the list's tab, click "Add Entry", fill in the form, and click "OK":
  - Action: Permit or Deny.
  - Protocol (extended lists only): IP (any protocol), TCP, UDP, ICMP, or Other, by protocol number 0 to 255.
  - Source, and Destination (extended lists only): Any; Host, one address such as `192.168.1.10`; or Network, an address and prefix length such as `192.168.1.0/24`. The network address must have no host bits set: `192.168.1.0/24`, not `192.168.1.5/24`.
  - Source port and Destination port (TCP and UDP only): Any port, Equal to, Range, Greater than or Less than, with port numbers 1 to 65535. The SSH 22, DNS 53, HTTP 80 and HTTPS 443 buttons fill in the destination port. The destination port is the service being reached; the source port is usually left as Any port.
  - Match (TCP and UDP only): All packets; Established connections only (TCP: packets with ACK or RST, so replies to connections already open); or Replies to connections this device opened.
  - Seq: optional. Leave it empty to add the entry after the last one (its Seq + 10). A Seq the list already has is refused.
  - "Entry" at the bottom shows the line the form builds, in the device's syntax.
- To type the entry in Cisco syntax instead, turn on "Type the entry" at the bottom left of the dialog. It starts from what the form has built.
  - Standard entry: permit or deny, then a source: `any`, `host 203.0.113.66`, or a network such as `198.51.100.0/24` (a wildcard mask, `198.51.100.0 0.0.0.255`, works too).
  - Extended entry: permit or deny, a protocol (`ip`, `tcp`, `udp`, `icmp`, or a number), a source, an optional source port, a destination, an optional destination port, and optionally `established` (TCP) or `reply` (TCP or UDP), for example `permit tcp 192.168.1.0/24 any eq 22`. Ports: `eq N`, `range LO HI`, `gt N`, `lt N`.
- There is no Edit: to change an entry, add the new one and delete the old one. To put an entry between two others, give it a Seq between theirs (for example 15 between 10 and 20).
- Delete an entry: click "Delete" on its row and confirm.
- Delete a list: click "Delete List" on its tab and confirm. A list that an interface applies can't be deleted; remove it from the interface first.
- If the device refuses a change, its reason is shown as it is, for example "access list 100 already has sequence 10" or "access list 100 is applied to eth0; remove it there first".

### Interfaces

- Columns: Interface, Lists applied (incoming), Actions. Next to the name, "Filtered" means the engine is filtering it now; "Not on this device" means no such interface exists.
- Apply a list: click "Apply List" (on the interface's row, or at the top right of the card for an interface not listed yet), enter the interface name, for example `eth0`, choose the list, and click "OK". It replaces the list of the same kind (standard or extended) the interface applied.
- Stop applying a list: click the × on its tag in "Lists applied" and choose "Remove".
- Delete: click "Delete" on the row and confirm. The interface stops applying all its lists.

### Examples

- Allow SSH only from the office network `192.168.1.0/24`, on eth0:
  1. Click "New List", enter 100 and click "OK".
  2. On tab 100, click "Add Entry": Action Permit, Protocol TCP, Source Network `192.168.1.0/24`, Destination Any, Destination port SSH 22. Click "OK".
  3. Add Entry: Action Deny, Protocol TCP, Source Any, Destination Any, Destination port SSH 22.
  4. Add Entry: Action Permit, Protocol IP (any protocol), Source Any, Destination Any, so other traffic still passes.
  5. In Interfaces, click "Apply List", enter `eth0`, choose 100, and click "OK".
  6. Click "Save Config".
- Block one malicious host on eth0 with a standard list: create list 10, add an entry with Action Deny and Source Host `203.0.113.66`, apply list 10 to eth0, and click "Save Config". Other traffic still goes through, since a standard list only drops what it denies.

## Saving the configuration

- Access list changes take effect at once but live only in the device's running state. The "Unsaved changes" tag in the header means the running configuration differs from the one the device loads when it starts.
- "Save Config" saves the running configuration, so the device loads it at its next start, and the "Unsaved changes" tag goes away.
- If you undo a change by hand, the tag goes away too, since the configuration matches the saved one again.
- Only administrators can save the configuration.

## Common questions

- I added an entry but the traffic isn't blocked. Check that an interface applies the list (Interfaces); that no permit entry with a lower Seq in the same list matches the traffic first; that the addresses, protocol and port are right; and that the ACL Engine card says "Enforced". Watch whether "Dropped (packets)" goes up.
- All my traffic is blocked after I applied an extended list. In an extended list, traffic that matches no entry is dropped, so end the list with a permit entry for the rest, such as `permit ip any any`. A standard list doesn't do this: it only drops what it denies.
- I can't see the access lists. Your account is a user, not an administrator; only administrators can view or change them.
- My rules were gone after the device restarted. The changes weren't saved with "Save Config". Ask an administrator to save after making changes.
- I can't see the "Save Config" button. Your account is a user, not an administrator; ask an administrator to save.
- "Network error. Please try again later." The browser can't reach the device. Check your network connection and reload the page.
- "Request failed" or another error after an action. Try again later; if it keeps happening, contact the administrator.
